description:
Build the recorded-failure corpus inside the suite through the input-keyed fixture cache, so the default suite runs no nested cargo test and the runner configuration names no test.

## Background

`.config/nextest.toml` runs `scripts/setup-recorded-failure-corpus.sh` as the `recorded-failure-corpus` setup script for three named `cli_issue` tests: `failure_envelope_contract_tests::test_recorded_failure_arms_emit_the_canonical_error_envelope`, `failure_probe_coverage_tests::test_failure_probe_coverage_matches_clap_arms_and_emits_typed_envelopes` and `payload_stream_purity_tests::test_machine_readable_failures_emit_one_json_document_on_payload_stream`. Inside the suite run, the script runs a nested `cargo test --workspace --test cli_issue` of `failure_probe_fixture::test_failure_probe_fixture_accepts_every_recorded_setup_step` to publish a receipt. `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/failure_probe_fixture.rs:1060-1075` runs the script's `--self-test` and parses the nextest configuration, and `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` pins the nextest version the script checks. The failure-lever registry is `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/failure_lever_registry.toml`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The three corpus consumers obtain the recorded-failure corpus through the input-keyed fixture cache. It is built in-process on first use and keyed on the failure-lever registry bytes and the crate source digest.
- [hard] REQ-02: `scripts/setup-recorded-failure-corpus.sh`, its setup-script declaration and its test-name filter no longer exist, and no test runs the script.
- [hard] REQ-03: The default suite runs no nested cargo invocation for the corpus.
- [hard] REQ-04: The registered `cargo-ci-selftest` gate no longer lists `scripts/setup-recorded-failure-corpus.sh` among its inputs; the path is dropped in the same change that deletes the script.
- [hard] REQ-05: The three consumers assert what they asserted before.
title: Recorded-failure corpus built in the suite under an input key
